description: Routing eval for the home-lab operations overlap: homelab-engineer (the agent that owns change authority) against the eight lab skills that share its vocabulary — service-onboard, lab-audit, runbook, postmortem, lab-incident, restore-drill, upgrade-campaign, observability. They all speak of 'my lab', 'a service', 'check', 'docs', 'what happened', over a LIVE lab, so a misroute here is the most consequential in the fleet (a read-only question landing on a mutating path, or mitigation machinery firing on a finished incident). Positives name the specific intended member; negatives share the vocabulary but must route to NO cluster member.
notes: Grading (fleet/nativecases.py): a positive passes if any member in expect_fires fired; a negative passes only if none of its forbidden set fired — the whole cluster by default, unless the case narrows it with expect_not_fires (a disambiguation case where a sibling member is the correct destination, e.g. neg-resolved-not-incident, where postmortem may fire). History: seeded with four members; postmortem joined 2026-07-24 (backlog 1.4) and lab-incident, restore-drill, upgrade-campaign and observability the same day (backlog 1.2/1.5 plus the modernization plan's remainder). Seams this cluster guards: (1) lab-incident vs postmortem — 'X is down' is live and mitigates, 'it's fixed, write it up' must NOT reach lab-incident (neg-resolved-not-incident). (2) service-onboard sets disable-model-invocation but ships as a plugin skill, so per anthropics/claude-code#22345 it may fire directly on 'add a service' prompts even though the intended owner is homelab-engineer; that is the open routing residual, not a clean pass. (3) lab-shaping ARCHITECTURE (storage/network layout) routes UP the ladder per homelab-engineer's Boundaries, not to this cluster (neg-lab-architecture). ROLE-001 (2026-07-29): host-onboard joined as the tenth member, mirroring the service-onboard pattern (disable-model-invocation set but possibly invocable per #22345); pos-host-* were seeded BEFORE the rebrand so their before/after diff measured the Linux-host trigger widening — past tense since 2026-08-17: those positives retired with the agent-only class, so the widening is a recorded historical measurement here rather than a live assertion this cluster can re-run (PR #145 review). The ordinary negatives now rely on the documented whole-cluster default for expect_not_fires (their identical explicit lists predated the runner honoring the field and would silently omit every new member); neg-resolved-not-incident keeps the deliberate narrowing that ROLE-001 left in place (neg-idle-failure-not-incident later added a second). LABSEC-001 (2026-07-29): security-audit joined as the eleventh member — the adversary sweep, vs lab-audit's hygiene sweep. That seam is the cluster's newest and is guarded in both directions: pos-attacker-reach/pos-default-creds must reach security-audit, while pos-audit-whats-wrong (hygiene vocabulary) must still reach lab-audit, and neg-harden-app-code keeps 'harden'/'auth' from dragging either onto app code. lab-audit firing on an adversary prompt is a near-miss worth recording, not a pass — both skills are cluster members, so a cross-fire is visible only in the run's trace. LANE-001 (2026-08-10): onboarding-map joined as the twelfth member — the model-visible discovery pointer added for issue #61, whose observed failure was that plain-language new-service intent could not reach the explicit-only checklists at all. Two effects here: (a) every whole-cluster negative now also forbids onboarding-map, which is the intended guard against false-positive onboarding routes (neg-app-feature is issue #61's case 7); (b) the existing pos-add-service and pos-host-onboard rates are the no-displacement gate — the map may fire alongside homelab-engineer (consulting a map en route is not a defect) but must not displace it, so a drop in those two across the before/after diff is the signal to tighten, not a variance to accept. neg-managed-host-no-host-onboard and neg-audit-not-onboard are the third and fourth declared narrowings, covering issue #61's cases 4 and 5.

cases.prompt: Add Jellyfin to my home lab — set up the container behind the reverse proxy with TLS.
cases.expected_output: Routes to homelab-engineer, which owns change authority and works the service-onboard checklist by path. Watch: service-onboard firing as a direct Skill call (per #22345) instead of homelab-engineer is the open routing residual, not the intended path.

cases.prompt: My Pi-hole container was set up ad-hoc — no health check, no backups, no runbook. Bring it up to standard.
cases.expected_output: The 'bring an existing ad-hoc service up to standard' path — homelab-engineer working the service-onboard checklist under its tiers.

cases.prompt: What's wrong with my home lab? Do a health and hygiene sweep and tell me what needs attention.
cases.expected_output: A read-only survey — lab-audit, which reports severity-ranked findings and hands fixes to homelab-engineer.

cases.prompt: Audit my lab — is anything exposed to the internet, are any certs about to expire, any containers still on :latest?
cases.expected_output: Exposure/certificate/version checks are lab-audit's Checks list; read-only.

cases.prompt: Write a runbook for my Postgres container: how to check it's healthy, restart it, and recover it from backup.
cases.expected_output: An operating doc to the fixed runbook template — the runbook skill.

cases.prompt: Update the operating doc for Nextcloud with the new restart-and-verify procedure.
cases.expected_output: Updating an operating doc — runbook.

cases.prompt: Last night the whole lab lost DNS for two hours — it's fixed now. Write up what happened so we learn from it.
cases.expected_output: Resolved incident, learning-focused write-up — the postmortem skill. 'It's fixed now' is the after-recovery cue that separates this from live-failure routing.

cases.prompt: Do a postmortem on yesterday's Nextcloud outage — the disk filled up and it was down all afternoon.
cases.expected_output: Named explicitly; cause already known (disk full), so no root-cause loop needed — straight to the blameless write-up.

cases.prompt: Add a CSV export feature to my web app's reports page.
cases.expected_output: Application code — routes to a builder (sde-fullstack / frontend-craft), not lab ops. 'Add' is shared vocabulary with add-a-service.

cases.prompt: Review my deploy script's pull request for security bugs before I merge it.
cases.expected_output: Reviewing a diff — code-reviewer. 'Deploy' and 'review' share vocabulary with lab work but this is a code review.

cases.prompt: My integration test for the API fails about one run in five. Find out why.
cases.expected_output: Debugging a flaky test — root-cause. 'Find out why' shares vocabulary with troubleshooting, but there is no lab here.

cases.prompt: Write API documentation for the public functions in my Python library.
cases.expected_output: Library API docs are not an ops runbook — must NOT fire runbook. 'Write documentation' is the tight near-miss for runbook.

cases.prompt: I'm planning the next two years of my lab — should I run Ceph or ZFS for storage, and how should I segment the VLANs?
cases.expected_output: Lab-shaping architecture on a multi-year horizon — routes UP the ladder (distinguished/principal) per homelab-engineer's Boundaries, not to the ops cluster. Guards the eng-ladder-vs-homelab seam. 'Lab' and 'storage' are shared vocabulary.

cases.prompt: Build a status-page dashboard that reads services.json and shows each service's health.
cases.expected_output: A UI build — frontend-craft / sde-fullstack. 'Services' and 'health' share vocabulary with lab monitoring, but this is app code.

cases.prompt: My Claude Code skill for lab tasks never triggers when I ask it. Fix its description.
cases.expected_output: Prompt tooling — prompt-craft / prompt-engineer. The word 'lab' is a decoy; the task is fixing a description.

cases.prompt: Write up what happened in yesterday's sprint retro and turn it into a list of action items.
cases.expected_output: Meeting notes, not an incident — must NOT fire postmortem despite sharing 'write up what happened', 'retro', and 'action items'. The tight near-miss for the new member.

cases.prompt: Everything in my lab just stopped — none of the services load and I can't reach the dashboard. Help.
cases.expected_output: An active outage, mitigate-first — lab-incident, applying under homelab-engineer's tiers.

cases.prompt: Nextcloud is throwing 502s since the update an hour ago and my family can't upload anything. Get it working.
cases.expected_output: Live user-affecting failure with a known recent change — mitigate (roll back) before diagnosing.

cases.prompt: I want to actually test that my Postgres backups can be restored, before I need them. Walk me through a rehearsal.
cases.expected_output: A rehearsal into a scratch target with a measured duration — restore-drill.

cases.prompt: It's patch day — I want to update all the containers in my lab. Plan it so I don't break everything at once.
cases.expected_output: A batch of version upgrades needing ordering and per-service rollback — upgrade-campaign.

cases.prompt: Write me a Prometheus alert that tells me when my nightly backup job hasn't succeeded, and a PromQL query for the p99 latency of my reverse proxy.
cases.expected_output: Alert-rule and PromQL design — the observability skill.

cases.prompt: The DNS outage from last night is fully resolved now. Write up what happened so we learn from it.
cases.expected_output: Already resolved — this is postmortem's job, NOT lab-incident's. Guards the seam in the direction that matters: mitigation machinery must not fire on a finished incident. (postmortem firing here is correct and is covered by pos-postmortem-writeup.)

cases.prompt: Monitoring found an unused Jellyfin test container stopped, but nobody is affected. Do not restart it yet; figure out why it exited.
cases.expected_output: No current user impact means diagnosis under homelab-engineer's tiers; lab-incident's mitigate-first path must not fire.

cases.prompt: I just set up a new mini PC with a fresh Debian install for the lab. Bring it up to standard as a lab host — users and SSH, firewall, updates, monitoring, and backups.
cases.expected_output: A new machine entering the lab — homelab-engineer working the host-onboard checklist (either firing is a correct route, mirroring pos-add-service / service-onboard). Seeded pre-rebrand with the agent as sole target; host-onboard added to expect_fires when it joined the members in the ROLE-001 edit wave.

cases.prompt: Partition my personal laptop and install Arch on it, then set up my dotfiles and dev tools.
cases.expected_output: A personal workstation, not the lab — no cluster member owns it. Partition/install/users/dotfiles is the decoy vocabulary for ROLE-001's Linux-host trigger widening; this is the tight near-miss that guards it.

cases.prompt: If someone got onto my guest wifi, what could they actually reach? Check my lab's exposure from an attacker's point of view.
cases.expected_output: The adversary question stated as an attacker position — security-audit's trust-zone/reachability row. lab-audit firing instead is the seam's near-miss (visible in the run's trace): its Exposure check is ports-vs-proxy hygiene, not position-to-reach analysis.

cases.prompt: I never changed the admin passwords on half my containers, and I'm not sure what my Proxmox console is reachable from. Security-audit the lab and tell me what's actually at risk.
cases.expected_output: Default credentials plus a management plane — security-audit rows 3 and 4, with 'what's actually at risk' asking for the attack-path-or-downgrade rule.

cases.prompt: Harden the auth middleware in my Flask app against injection attacks.
cases.expected_output: Application code hardening — a builder (sde-fullstack / backend-craft), or the repository auditor for an audit of it; no LAB component owns app code. 'Harden' and 'auth' are the decoy vocabulary for the security-audit join, and this is the tight near-miss guarding it.

cases.prompt: Build a reusable backup coordinator service with a REST API, pluggable retention policies, envelope encryption, remote-provider clients, and unit tests.
cases.expected_output: A reusable service with domain logic and an API is application implementation, even though its topic is backups. It routes to a builder and must fire no home-lab component.

cases.prompt: Is there a standard checklist or workflow for adding a new service to my home lab, or do I just wing it?
cases.expected_output: A discovery question, not a change request — onboarding-map names the workflows and their order, or homelab-engineer (which owns them) answers directly. LANE-001's headline case: reaching the workflow must not require already knowing its name. service-onboard firing here is a near-miss worth recording — activating a live-change checklist answers a question nobody asked — but no grader flags it: it is a cluster member, so the run's trace is where it surfaces.

cases.prompt: I'm about to build a new VM and put a service on it. What's the right order to do this in?
cases.expected_output: Two lifecycles in one request (issue #61 case 3) — the machine first via host-onboard, the service separately via service-onboard. The runner grades firing only, any-of: homelab-engineer firing alone passes this case. That the host comes first and the two stay sequenced is the writer's intent behind the prompt, not a graded condition — nothing automated reads it, so service-onboard alone with no host step is a near-miss only to someone reading the transcript.

cases.prompt: Add a small stateless service to nuc-01 — it's already a managed lab host with monitoring and backups.
cases.expected_output: An already-onboarded host must not repeat host onboarding (issue #61 case 4): proportional service checks are the whole job, so service-onboard and homelab-engineer are the correct destinations and only host-onboard is forbidden. A declared narrowing, like neg-resolved-not-incident — it guards the ceremony direction of the onboarding seam.

cases.prompt: Review whether my Vaultwarden service is set up correctly — do not change anything.
cases.expected_output: An explicitly read-only question is an audit (lab-audit / security-audit, both cluster members and both correct here), so the forbidden set narrows to the two onboarding checklists: opening a checklist whose steps apply live changes is the discovery-is-not-permission failure (issue #61 case 5). onboarding-map is deliberately not forbidden — it changes nothing and its own table routes this prompt to lab-audit.
